headline: US stocks closed lower as global bond selloff pushed Treasury yields to multiyear highs and semiconductor weakness dragged tech ahead of FOMC minutes and key earnings
raw_text:
- S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all finished lower, marking a third straight decline for the S&P 500 amid rising global yields
- Treasury yields hit multiyear highs amid a global bond selloff, pressuring equities and especially rate-sensitive growth and tech names
- PHLX Semiconductor Index fell sharply, with Micron (MU), Intel (INTC), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Seagate Technology (STX), Western Digital (WDC), and Sandisk (SNDK) declining amid rising yields, memory-chip weakness, and AI-related concerns
- Energy and healthcare sectors outperformed, with energy names including Targa Resources (TRGP) gaining after signing 20-year integrated midstream agreements with ExxonMobil
- Home Depot (HD) beats fiscal Q2 estimates and says tariff refunds will be fully offset by higher costs
- Amylyx Pharmaceuticals (AMLX) posted a sharp gain after its avexitide Phase 3 LUCIDITY trial met all endpoints, standing out among large individual movers
- Haemonetics (HAE) advanced by double digits after announcing a new CSL Plasma supply agreement, adding to strength in select healthcare names
- After-hours trading was subdued with no notable stock moves exceeding roughly 2%, including only modest reactions in Western Digital (WDC)
- Investors turned attention to Wednesday’s FOMC minutes, further debt and bond-market developments, and earnings from Analog Devices (ADI), TJX (TJX), Lowe’s (LOW), Target (TGT), and Estée Lauder
